commits.edited_message:
Let color-conversion operators declare the sample width they read

The operators picked uint8_t or uint16_t samples from an 8-bit SDR/HDR split
(bits_per_pixel > 8 meant "two bytes per sample"). That dates from when 16 bits
was the maximum and is wrong for the 32-, 64- and 128-bit components that
'unci' can carry: HeifPixelImage stores those with 4, 8 or 16 bytes per sample.
Nothing wider than 16 bits could reach an operator, because each of them
guarded against it separately through has_samples_wider_than_16bit() and
convert_colorspace() has a backstop, but the sample type never followed the
allocation, so those guards were load-bearing.

Make the sample width explicit instead. bytes_per_sample_for_bit_depth() in
pixelimage.h is now the single mapping from bit depth to storage width, used
by plane allocation and by the operators, so the two cannot drift. ColorState
gained get_bytes_per_sample(), get_max_bytes_per_sample(),
color_channels_have_bytes_per_sample() and all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(),
and each operator declares in state_after_conversion() which width it can read
(sizeof(Pixel) for the templated ones, 1 or 2 for the others). Strides are
divided by the sample width instead of by a conditional 2, alpha rows are
copied with their own width, and the operators that switch on the width at
runtime refuse anything else. has_samples_wider_than_16bit() and the
all_channels_sdr()/all_channels_hdr() helpers have no callers left and are
removed; the check added for GHSA-r7gr-2xm2-23wf in Op_flatten_alpha_plane
becomes all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(sizeof(Pixel)).

The 16-bit backstop and the YCbCr luma/chroma check in convert_colorspace()
now also run when no pipeline could be built, so callers keep getting the
specific error instead of the generic "unsupported color conversion". The
RRGGBBaa operator's own luma/chroma check duplicates that entry check and is
dropped with the other redundant runtime guards.

A new test builds 32-, 64- and 128-bit YCbCr, RGB and monochrome states and
checks that the operators decline them and that no pipeline is constructible.

Declare the shared colour depth in the YCbCr operators, drop the backstop

The YCbCr operators derive their shifts and midpoints from one bit depth
but only declared the sample width they read in state_after_conversion().
A YCbCr image whose planes differ in depth ('unci' declares a depth per
component) was therefore kept away from them by a blanket check at the
entry of convert_colorspace() (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), which also refused
conversions that would have been safe: Op_to_sdr_planes lowers every plane
on its own and can equalize such an image to 8 bits, as it already did for
RGB. YCbCr 16/16/8 to 8-bit RGB was refused while RGB 16/16/8 converted.

Op_YCbCr_to_RGB and the four chroma-sampling operators now require
color_channels_have_same_bpp() at plan time (their runtime guards already
returned InternalError for mixed depths), and the two 8-bit 4:2:0-to-RGB
operators test the uniform colour depth instead of the luma depth alone.
With the YCbCr operators declaring the constraint, the entry check is
removed; the wider-than-16-bit backstop stays.

The GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps requiring a clean refusal for the
reporter's 16-bit target (no operator can widen the 8-bit chroma planes),
now with the generic Unsupported_color_conversion subcode, and adds the two
8-bit routes that succeed: interleaved RGB, and the native layout with
convert_hdr_to_8bit, whose samples are checked exactly.

coupling:
Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa (libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc) converts YCbCr 4:2:0 to 16-bit interleaved RGB; it takes its sample width from the luma depth and reads the Cb/Cr planes through a uint16_t*. A YCbCr image whose planes declare different depths (an 'unci' item may declare a depth per component, e.g. 16-bit luma with 8-bit chroma) is only kept safe by three independent layers, and the two edited commits each remove one layer while a third is removed believing the others remain.

Edit in 4c072c8 (sample-width declarations): (i) the operator's new plan-time declaration caps planes at the uint16_t width (get_max_bytes_per_sample() > 2) instead of requiring every plane at exactly 2 bytes/sample, so a 16/8/8 image passes planning; (ii) the operator's runtime luma/chroma bit-depth guard is dropped as redundant with the YCbCr luma/chroma check in convert_colorspace() - a check that genuinely still exists at that point in history, so this commit's tree is safe and the removal is correct maintenance in isolation.

Edit in 35ffaa8 (drop the backstop): the convert_colorspace() entry check is removed (as the real commit intends) and plan-time uniform-depth declarations are added to Op_YCbCr_to_RGB, the four chroma-sampling operators and the two 8-bit 4:2:0 operators - but the 16-bit RRGGBBaa operator keeps its pre-existing luma-only test (bits_per_pixel_Y <= 8), which the diff simply leaves untouched. In isolation this is also safe: the original 4c072c8 code still declares all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(2) for that operator and the runtime guard still rejects a mismatch, so no pipeline is built for a 16/8/8 image.

Only the composition is defective: luma test passes (16 > 8), no uniform-depth declaration, no exact-width declaration, no runtime guard, no entry backstop - the operator runs on a 16-bit luma / 8-bit chroma image and reads every chroma row twice as wide as the 1-byte/sample plane, a heap-buffer-overflow read past each chroma plane (ASan: READ of size 2 at the end of the chroma plane allocation, reached via heif_decode_image).

A correct fix is non-local: neither edited diff contains the defect. 4c072c8's edits are correct against the entry check that exists when it lands; 35ffaa8's diff never touches the RRGGBBaa condition (the luma-only test is pre-existing code) and is correct against the exact-width declaration and runtime guard that exist when it lands. Finding the hole requires reasoning about the operator's guard state across both commits, and patching only one commit's diff (e.g. only restoring the entry-check comment in 35ffaa8, or only the message-level redundancy claim in 4c072c8) leaves the operator reachable; safety is only restored by re-establishing a uniform/exact-width declaration or a runtime guard for this specific operator, which no single edited diff shows.

pocs.entry_point: heif_decode_image (libheif public C API; input built in-memory and parsed via heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy)
